title: Primer
scope: The 2004 film · the basic first-box method only
premise: Abe cannot simply dial a date into his machine. Returning to an earlier point requires the box to have been running—and requires him to spend time inside it.
ending: The box connects a later entry to an earlier exit within its operating interval. Abe’s preparation prevents his earlier self from casually meeting the returning traveller. Later failsafes and competing plans are deliberately outside this guide.

people.name: Abe
people.introduction: An engineer demonstrating the first method of travelling with the box.

events.title: Start the box to establish how far back it can reach
events.text: Abe arranges for the box to start running. It cannot take him back to a time before it was operating.

events.title: Keep the earlier self out of the way
events.text: Abe isolates himself while the day passes. This gives the version who will emerge earlier a window in which to act without immediately meeting him.

events.title: Enter the box later
events.text: Later, Abe enters the running box. Travelling back takes time inside it: he must experience the duration of the trip.

events.title: Emerge near the beginning of its run
events.text: After the journey through the box, Abe exits at an earlier point in the machine’s operating interval. His experienced order has moved from the later entry to the earlier exit.
events.whenLabel: Earlier on the calendar · later in Abe’s experience

events.title: Two stages of Abe now share the day
events.text: The returned Abe can act during the same interval when his earlier self is still keeping out of the way. Both are Abe, at different stages of his life. This is the overlap made possible by the preparation described earlier.

chapters.title: Understand the overlap
chapters.introduction: Look again at the interval when Abe waited. This final card explains who is present during that interval; it is not an extra step later on the calendar.

sources.title: Repository story record
sources.note: Editorial pilot adapted from the repository. Scene wording and interpretation await a separate review against the primary work.

sources.title: Shane Carruth explains the machine’s limits
sources.note: IEEE Spectrum’s interview asks how the machines operate. The question identifies the start-time limit; Carruth explains that travellers must experience the duration inside. It does not verify Abe’s exact preparation or timings in the released film.

connections.label: Abe enters later and emerges earlier within the box’s operating interval.

flowchart.title: Timeline flow chart
flowchart.description: The loop arrow connects the later entry to the earlier exit. Waiting, emerging and overlap are explanatory cards for overlapping portions of the day, not three successive dates. Only the basic method is shown.
flowchart.frame: Abe’s preparation and the overlapping interval, arranged by the explanation rather than an exact clock.

timelines.description: The timeline already exists within this guide’s stated scope.
